label: input f at a late original position (orig_idx 6-8)
explanation: Fires when the input token is f during the original phase at positions 6, 7 or 8 (only sequences with L >= 7). Precision is 1.0 on dev: every late-position f activates it. It is strongest when f is the last original token, right before <DEL> (to_go=0 holds about 65% of the mass and the top examples are near max). It is weaker with 1-2 tokens still to come (to_go=2 activations are around 0.13-0.25 of max). It never fires on f at positions 0-5, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase. The leftover misses are tiny activations (<0.06 of max) on input d at step 8, about 0.4% of the mass.

issues: Every factual claim held up. On dev the feature never fires on the delimiter or in the copy phase (0 active). It only fires at t=6-8 and only when L>=7. f accounts for 99.6% of the activation mass. to_go 0/1/2 hold 0.645/0.288/0.068 of the mass, so the claim that about 65% sits at to_go=0 is correct.
On test the predicate has 0 false positives, and the scores match the report exactly: P 1.0, R 0.951, F1 0.975, mass recall 0.996.
The f/to_go==2 slice has a test mass recall of 0.07 over 15.9% of active steps. That puts its mean activation at about 0.18 of max, which matches the 0.13-0.25 claim.

Not every miss is noise: most are input d at step 8 (the last original position, L=9). This is a small systematic class, but those activations are all <=0.05 of max and hold 0.4% of the mass. Adding it would barely change the score, so it is not worth adding to the predicate. Minor overclaim: d also fires in the bottom activation quartile, so 'f only' is accurate in mass but not in count (bottom-quartile coverage is 0.80).
